title: October: Growing Up and Apart
coreMove: Use a social pressure audit to tell awkward adjustment from contempt, then keep the friends who respect the ban and set limits around pressure.

exampleSpecs.audience: Whitney, a writer making a private ban public
exampleSpecs.stakes: A sincere accountability space can become a shame arena if hostile replies set the tone.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show that public change needs a boundary around the conversation it creates.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jasper, a friend protecting newer boundaries
exampleSpecs.stakes: A joke can either help the table adjust or ask him to return to an old role.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Connect the shopping ban to earlier social pushback around visible lifestyle changes.

exampleSpecs.audience: Philomene, a friend repairing a missed cue
exampleSpecs.stakes: Support can replace a consumption script before the person on the ban has to defend herself again.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show supportive friendship that does not treat the shopping ban as strange.

exampleSpecs.audience: Garrett, a friend separating closeness from purchases
exampleSpecs.stakes: The default route may be doing the pressure work before anyone says a word.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Separate genuine friendship from a spending loop that has become the group's script.

exampleSpecs.audience: Domenic, a person refusing to buy reassurance
exampleSpecs.stakes: A single remark can make appearance spending feel like safety again.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how wardrobe and dating criticism reveals consumer pressure around worth.

exampleSpecs.audience: Lorne, a traveler redirecting money toward experience
exampleSpecs.stakes: The ban can shrink buying while expanding connection.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show richer experience increasing while purchases decrease.
